texts.preamble: Mukesh Kumar Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 December, 2025 Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia Bench: G. S. Ahluwalia Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:33093 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice G. S. Ahluwalia On The 16 th Of December, 2025 Miscellaneous Second Appeal No. 12 of 2025 Mukesh Kumar Jain Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh Appearance: Shri Deependra Singh Raghuwanshi, Advocate for appellan Shri Sanjay Singh Kushwaha, Government Advocate for res Order
texts.facts: This miscellaneous second appeal, under Section 71(6) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short "the Act") has been filed against the order dated 08.01.2025 passed by the appellate Authority/ IX th District Judge, Gwalior in RCA No. 346 of 2024, as well as, order dated 24.10.2024 passed by the Adjudicating Officer/ Additional District Magistrate, Gwalior in Case No. Q/Food Safety/114/2024. 2. Facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short, are that on 17.08.2023 at about 3:15 p.m., Food Safety Officer inspected the shop of the appellant and found that 4 kg of Chhaina, 3 kg of milk cake, 5 kg of Peda and 3 kg of food product meant for human consumption were stored for the purpose of sale, and 5 kg of sugar, Maida etc. were also found for production of aforesaid food articles. Since the Food Safety Officer had an apprehension that loose Barfi and loose Khoya may be of substandard quality, therefore, samples were collected. One sample each was sent to the Food Analyst, Bhopal and as per the report of Food Analyst, Barfi and Khoya were found to be of substandard quality. The NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:33093 2 MSA-12-2025 report of Food Analyst was sent to appellant by registered post, but no appeal was filed for getting the aforesaid samples tested from the referral laboratory. Accordingly, a complaint was filed. 3. The evidence of the Food Safety Officer was recorded. 4. Being aggrieved by the said order, appellant preferred an appeal which has been dismissed by judgment dated 08.01.2025. However, the penalty was reduced and penalty of Rs. 2 lac awarded under Section 51 of the Act was reduced to Rs. 1 lac and the penalty of Rs. 1 lac awarded under Section 52 was reduced to Rs. 50,000/-. 5. Challenging the orders passed by the appellate authority and the adjudicating authority, it is submitted by counsel for appellant that there is nothing on record to show that the report of Food Analyst was ever received by the appellant. Appellant had specifically stated in his written statement that report of Food Analyst was never supplied to him and, accordingly, he could not prefer any appeal.
texts.arguments: 10. Section 27 of the General Clauses Act reads as under:- "27. Meaning of service by post. Where any Central Act or Regulation made after the commencement of this Act authorizes or requires any document to be served by post, whether the expression "serve" or either of the expressions "give" or "send" or any other expression is used, then, unless a different intention appears, the service shall be deemed to be effected by properly addressing, pre-paying and posting by registered post, a letter containing the document, and, unless the contrary is proved, to have been effected at the time at which the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post." Mukesh Kumar Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65317347/ 2 11. Thus, if registered letter is dispatched with complete address of the addressee, as well as, with proper postal stamp and if the acknowledgement is not received back within a period of 30 days, then it shall be presumed that the registered letter has been served. Counsel for appellant could not point out any judgment passed by the Supreme Court to the effect that in spite of Section 27 of the General NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:33093 4 MSA-12-2025 Clauses Act, the prosecution is under an obligation to prove that the report of Food Analyst was actually served on the appellant. 12.
